question.question: Can subscribe_decided emit a retained decided entry after a later log entry has already been emitted when catch-up begins inside a compacted prefix?
question.importance: A stream that moves backward can cause application consumers to replay earlier state changes after later ones even while consensus decisions remain stable.
participants: Quorum peers that establish the log
contexts: Fixed cluster with stable decided log

supporting_behavior_ids.b-formation: Establishes the decided history consumed by this supporting-layer behavior.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-read: Defines compacted-prefix summary plus suffix vector representation.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-compaction: Creates the summary and retained suffix through public compaction API.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-runtime-loop: Schedules catch-up command and later periodic fanout.

counterevidence: Without compaction, vector positions correspond to original log positions and per-send increments are appropriate.
read_decided_suffix intentionally returns a snapshot marker; absence of compacted individual entries is not itself a defect.
Full subscriber channels defer pushes and can change observed timing; a check must drain the receiver.
unknowns: Need an executed public-API history linking a legal snapshot, initial catch-up and a later backward transition among retained decided entries.
question.trigger_rationale: The subscribe_decided interface explicitly promises log order. Read output collapses multiple compacted positions into one marker, while both push paths increment cursor by one per marker or entry. A small stable-cluster check isolates this producer/consumer mismatch without uncertain fault contracts; another notifier variant would not address an independent requirement.

obligation.description: Within one subscribe_decided stream over a stable decided log, emitted retained Decided entries must preserve their original log order: an entry from an earlier position must not follow an emitted entry from a later position.

scope.description: One accepted subscription starting before an already compacted prefix, with a nonempty retained decided suffix, no concurrent changes to log decisions or compaction, and an actively drained subscriber.
assumptions: Valid fixed membership and reliable in-memory storage.
Unique entry values allow independent mapping of emitted entries to previously observed original log positions.
Runtime timers and channel receiver are driven.
excluded: No requirement to re-emit individual entries removed by compaction.
No claim that a snapshot marker is itself an ordinary single-position entry.
No deadline or unbounded eventual-delivery claim.

grounding.derivation: The public subscription documentation states that LogEntry values are emitted in log order, including historical and future decisions. The existing history/live test corroborates ordered suffix consumption. The selected obligation only forbids reversal among retained entries whose original positions are independently known; it neither demands missing compacted entries nor assumes one snapshot equals one log position.
grounding.applicability: Successful subscription below capacity; preexisting snapshot is a legal core state supplied to spawn_actor. A snapshot-prefix subscription is not excluded by the public interface.
unresolved: Need actual stream observations to establish whether cursor interpretation produces a reversal.

bindings.description: Consumes subscriber cursor as original-log/vector offset and increments it for every successfully enqueued representation.

associations.rationale: Periodic fanout continues the same stream after catch-up and implements the ordered subscription responsibility.
